My work is centred on economic geography, spatial inequality, and urban economics. Transport networks provide one setting in which I study how changes in connectivity affect places and populations.

## Master's thesis

### The Political Consequences of Infrastructure Withdrawal Electoral Effects of Railway Station Closures in France

**Completed June 2026**  
Supervisor: Camille Hémet · Université Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne and Paris School of Economics

This thesis examines the relationship between changes in access to passenger railway stations and French electoral outcomes in the late 1960s and early 1970s. It brings together historical railway-station data, electoral returns, commune characteristics, and measures of accessibility. The thesis does not claim definitive causal findings.
